title: Snapshot
body:
## The Platform and Its Wager

POET Technologies entered fiscal 2025 as it had entered every prior year of its modern iteration: without commercial revenue, without named customers, and without a product embedded in any hyperscaler supply chain. What changed by December 31 was the capitalisation behind the wager. The company closed the year with [$313.4 million of cash and short-term investments](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results) — up from $53.8 million twelve months earlier — funded by a $250 million institutional equity raise from three undisclosed buyers. Against a net loss of $62.96 million and full-year revenue of approximately $1.2 million in non-recurring engineering fees and small product receipts, POET stood as one of the purest option-value propositions in the photonics equity universe.

The company is incorporated in Toronto, Ontario, with its wafer-level photonic integration line operated through POET Singapore Pte. Ltd. It carried a dual listing — NASDAQ and the Toronto Stock Exchange, both under the ticker POET — and filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on a 20-F basis as a foreign private issuer. That designation is not merely administrative: it determines disclosure cadence, governance standards, and the institutional machinery through which POET accesses capital across two markets.

## The Architecture

POET designed and licensed the POET Optical Interposer: a wafer-level photonic integration platform built around a passive substrate hosting multiple optical components — lasers, modulators, photodetectors, and filters — with minimal optical coupling loss. The platform targeted 800G and 1.6 terabit transceiver applications and positioned specifically for co-packaged optics (CPO) and external light source (ELS) modules, the two segments of the hyperscaler interconnect stack where component architecture remained most architecturally open at the snapshot date.

The interposer thesis rested on integration density and coupling efficiency. POET argued that assembling heterogeneous optical components on a single passive substrate avoided the coupling losses endemic to silicon-photonics monolithic designs while enabling the chiplet-style disaggregation that hyperscalers increasingly demanded as co-packaged optics migrated from whiteboard to rack.

## The People Calibrated for This Bet

Dr. Suresh Venkatesan has served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer since 2015. He came to POET from GlobalFoundries, where as Senior Vice President of Technology Development he led the 28nm process ramp and was instrumental in the 14nm technology transfer — the competitive inflection at which GlobalFoundries, Samsung, and TSMC most acutely contested process leadership. Before GlobalFoundries he held multiple leadership positions at Freescale Semiconductor and was named a Freescale Fellow in 2007 for CMOS technology contributions. He holds a Ph.D. in electrical engineering from Purdue University.

Jean-Louis Malinge, Lead Independent Director since September 2017, brought the board its most directly relevant operating precedent. Malinge ran Kotura — a silicon photonics pioneer whose products reached three of the top five global telecom companies — from 2004 until its [sale to Mellanox in 2013 for $82 million](https://www.poet-technologies.com/team/jean-louis-malinge), subsequently joining ARCH Venture Partners as a partner. His presence signalled that at least one board member had lived the complete arc: build a photonics platform, qualify it into hyperscaler-adjacent supply chains, and deliver it into a larger semiconductor ecosystem. It is the closest available operational template for what POET was attempting.

## Financials at the Frozen Window

| FY2025 metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Revenue (NRE + product receipts) | ~$1.2M |
| Net loss | $62.96M |
| R&D expense | $18.08M |
| SG&A expense | $25.08M |
| Approx. non-cash operating costs | ~$35M |
| Cash and short-term investments | $313.4M |
| Total assets | $328.6M |
| Derivative warrant liability | $135.6M |
| Common shares outstanding | 132.3M |
| Options + warrants outstanding | 43.2M |
| Implied dilution on full exercise | ~28.4% |

The balance sheet transformation was the defining financial event of FY2025. Total assets grew from $69.7 million at December 2024 to $328.6 million at December 2025 — a near-fivefold expansion funded entirely by the institutional raise. The three buyers were not publicly disclosed at the snapshot date. On the liability side, a $135.6 million derivative warrant liability represented a mark-to-market obligation: non-cash in the current period but carrying real economic weight against the 37.36 million warrants outstanding. The accumulated deficit stood at approximately $297 million — the cumulative equity cost of the platform thesis to date.

At the FY2025 cash burn rate of roughly $45 million annually — net loss of $62.96 million less approximately $18 million of non-cash charges — the $313.4 million cash position implied approximately seven years of operational runway. POET's most recently disclosed strategic partnership, with Sivers Semiconductors announced in September 2025, centred on external light sources for co-packaged optics applications and was the most concrete third-party validation of the platform at the snapshot date. The FY2025 20-F explicitly noted no major customers, partners, or design wins by name.

## The Central Tension

The arithmetic was stark. POET's $1.2 million of FY2025 revenue did not cover a single week of its $18 million R&D run rate. The company had consumed approximately $297 million of cumulative equity through the close of FY2025 without reaching commercial scale. The $313 million cash position bought time — seven years at current burn — but not resolution. The board composition added texture to the governance framing: Venkatesan's foundry-process pedigree, Malinge's Kotura-to-Mellanox arc, Theresa Lan Ende's working seat as Arista Networks' Chief Procurement Officer, Glen Riley's 32 years across optoelectronics and GaAs foundry management, and Sohail Khan's Coherent silicon-carbide EVP credential collectively read as governance calibrated for precisely this transition. Whether the runway was long enough to cross from platform thesis to qualified component in hyperscaler CPO supply chains was the question the rest of this report existed to frame.
